fact: The Centre gabonais de l'innovation and UNDP signed a partnership in Libreville to launch TechSpace Masuku, a technology incubator at the Universite des sciences et techniques de Masuku, with a programme to train more than 300 young people; no cohort is yet reported.

L'Union reports on 27 August 2026 that the Societe d'incubation numerique du Gabon (SING) has not been closed but placed under interim management, and that its incubated companies and their projects depend on continued support during the transition.

GabonReview says SING SA, the state digital incubator in Libreville, runs the Pivot 4.0 incubation and acceleration programme and claims 314 startups supported since 2018, though its offices are reported emptied and a merger into the Centre gabonais de l'innovation is said to be under study.

GabonReview describes the Centre gabonais de l'innovation, under the digital economy ministry, as an innovation and technology hub at Batterie 4 in Libreville that could become the main public vehicle for startup support.
Kimba Connect, run from the Centre Gabonais de l'Innovation, reports 155 registered startups, 133 submissions to 16 challenges and 66 shortlisted, with pitches scheduled through August 2026 (AGP).
The minister says the Centre Gabonais de l'Innovation, an ITU Innovation Alliance member, incubates start-ups and has become a regional driver.
